issue.title: Record the imported git source revision on tui_startup rows without a subprocess

task_type_fields.proposal:
Add a `source_revision` field to `tui_startup.jsonl` records (`src/sase/ace/tui/actions/_startup_telemetry.py`, next to `sase_version` from `_cheap_sase_version()`). It should identify the git commit of the editable checkout the TUI process imported.

Do it without a subprocess. Read `<checkout>/.git/HEAD` and resolve the ref through `.git/<ref>` or `packed-refs`, following a `.git` file for worktrees. Capture the value once at import or construction time, so it reflects the imported snapshot rather than the checkout's current HEAD (tui_perf.md rule 15), and record `null` for non-git installs. Optionally add it to `tui_memory_heartbeat` rows too, so `tools/tui_freeze_report` can label each `app_instance_id` with its code revision.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Proposed by sase-1ez.1 (gc-telemetry, note #1). Epic sase-1ez's plan made this optional ("if it is cheap"). The phase only considered a `git` subprocess, rejected it as non-cheap on the startup path, and recorded `sase_version` instead. Per-instance identity, the thing the epic needed, is already covered by `app_instance_id`. Identifying which code an editable-install TUI imported is a separate observability improvement for later acceptance forensics.

issue.creation_reason: sase-1ez.1 deferred the optional source revision because it only considered a git subprocess; reading .git/HEAD directly would make it cheap and help tell which code an editable-install TUI is running.
